/-!
# Conjecture 10.42

by G. A. Noskov

(J. T. Stafford). Let $G$ be a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group and let $k$ be a field. Is it true
that every finitely generated projective $kG$-module is either a free module or an ideal?

A poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group is a group with a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
all of whose factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ are infinite cyclic. Modules are left $kG$-modules and
"is an ideal" means "is isomorphic, as a $kG$-module, to a left ideal of $kG$". Since the
modules in question are finitely generated, "free" automatically means free of finite rank.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsPolyZ (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, H i.castSucc ≤ H i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
        Nonempty ((H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)) ≃* Multiplicative ℤ)

A group $G$ is a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group if it has a finite subnormal series

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.IsSolvable / derivedSeries (wrong: solvable ≠ poly-ℤ), CompositionSeries via JordanHolderLattice on Subgroup (requires maximal/simple steps, ℤ is not simple), RelSeries (could have been used as a wrapper but gives no gain in clarity), IsCyclic ∧ Infinite for the factors (equivalent; ≃* Multiplicative ℤ chosen as the literal reading of "≅ ℤ").
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.42».IsPolyZ
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of polycyclic / poly-ℤ (poly-infinite-cyclic) groups, nor of subnormal series with prescribed factors. Defined as: ∃ n and H : Fin (n+1) → Subgroup G with H 0 = ⊥, H (Fin.last n) = ⊤, and for each i, H i.castSucc ≤ H i.succ, (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ) is normal, and the quotient H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ) is ≃* Multiplicative ℤ. Two proved @[category test] lemmas (trivial group; Multiplicative ℤ) exercise it.

theorem isPolyZ_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPolyZ G :=

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolyZ_multiplicative_int : IsPolyZ (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  exact ⟨bot_le, inferInstance, ⟨(QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq
    (Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf _)).trans (QuotientGroup.quotientBot.trans Subgroup.topEquiv)⟩⟩

@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (k : Type) [Field k], IsPolyZ G →
      ∀ (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MonoidAlgebra k G) P]
        [Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra k G) P] [Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra k G) P],
        Module.Free (MonoidAlgebra k G) P ∨
          ∃ I : Ideal (MonoidAlgebra k G), Nonempty (P ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra k G] I) := by

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question quantified over all poly-ℤ groups G (groups with a finite subnormal series with all factors ≅ ℤ — the convention must be fixed, e.g. subnormal vs normal series) and all fields k; 'module' must be fixed as left (or right) kG-module, 'free' means free of finite rank, and 'is an ideal' means isomorphic as a kG-module to a (left) ideal of the group ring kG, so the Prop is ∀ G k, ∀ f.g. projective kG-module P, P is free ∨ ∃ left ideal I ≤ kG with P ≃ₗ[kG] I.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ poly-ℤ group G : Type, ∀ field k : Type, ∀ f.g. projective left module P over MonoidAlgebra k G, P is free ∨ ∃ left ideal I of kG with P ≃ₗ[kG] I. Their bespoke poly-ℤ predicates (Fin-indexed subnormal series with normal `subgroupOf` + quotient ≃* Multiplicative ℤ in c02/c03; surjection onto Multiplicative ℤ with kernel the previous term in c05–c08; recursive/inductive top-down in c01/c04) are all equivalent to the standard subnormal-series definition and all correctly include the trivial group via a length-0 series. `Module.Free` + `Module.Finite` is equivalent to the explicit `∃ n, P ≃ₗ Fin n → kG` of c05/c06 because kG is nontrivial (`Module.Finite.finite_basis`), so both 'free' encodings are faithful; Mathlib's `Ideal R = Submodule R R` is the left ideal, as the table fixes. c02 chosen as the cleanest: its definition is the literal textbook subnormal series, it includes tidy API tests for the bespoke definition (CONTRIBUTING asks for them; c05–c08 have none), and it follows the repo's `Type` binder idiom (c06 uses `Type*`). Shipped verbatim; compiles with only the sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.42

by G. A. Noskov

(J. T. Stafford). Let $G$ be a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group and let $k$ be a field. Is it true
that every finitely generated projective $kG$-module is either a free module or an ideal?

A poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group is a group with a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$
all of whose factors $G_{i+1}/G_i$ are infinite cyclic. Modules are left $kG$-modules and
"is an ideal" means "is isomorphic, as a $kG$-module, to a left ideal of $kG$". Since the
modules in question are finitely generated, "free" automatically means free of finite rank.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.42»

/--
A group $G$ is a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ in which every
factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}$.
-/
def IsPolyZ (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, H i.castSucc ≤ H i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
        Nonempty ((H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)) ≃* Multiplicative ℤ)

/-- The trivial group is a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group (with the series of length $0$). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolyZ_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPolyZ G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- The infinite cyclic group is a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolyZ_multiplicative_int : IsPolyZ (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩
  obtain rfl : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  exact ⟨bot_le, inferInstance, ⟨(QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq
    (Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf _)).trans (QuotientGroup.quotientBot.trans Subgroup.topEquiv)⟩⟩

/--
Let $G$ be a poly-$\mathbb{Z}$-group and let $k$ be a field. Is it true that every finitely
generated projective (left) $kG$-module is either a free module or isomorphic to a (left)
ideal of $kG$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (k : Type) [Field k], IsPolyZ G →
      ∀ (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MonoidAlgebra k G) P]
        [Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra k G) P] [Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra k G) P],
        Module.Free (MonoidAlgebra k G) P ∨
          ∃ I : Ideal (MonoidAlgebra k G), Nonempty (P ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra k G] I) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.42»

items: Poly-ℤ is defined with a SUBNORMAL series (each term normal in the next), the standard convention; the trivial group counts as poly-ℤ via the length-0 series (consistent with the usual convention, and harmless: kG = k then, and all f.g. modules are free).

Modules are left kG-modules (Mathlib's `Module R P`) and 'ideal' is a LEFT ideal (Mathlib's `Ideal R := Submodule R R`), consistently left-sided as the decomposition table requires; for group rings the left/right choice is immaterial via g ↦ g⁻¹.
'Is an ideal' is formalized as 'isomorphic as a kG-module to some left ideal of kG' (`Nonempty (P ≃ₗ[kG] I)`), per the table.
'Free' is `Module.Free (MonoidAlgebra k G) P`; together with `Module.Finite` this is automatically free of finite rank since kG is a nontrivial ring (k a field).
The group ring kG is `MonoidAlgebra k G`, as in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean.

All of G, k, P are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the repository idiom for answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ... statements; this loses no generality for the module P since it must be isomorphic to a submodule of kG : Type anyway, and for G, k it matches the other Kourovka files.
The factor condition uses `≃* Multiplicative ℤ` rather than `IsCyclic ∧ Infinite`; these are equivalent.

reviewer_notes: Conventions fixed as in the decomposition table: poly-ℤ = finite SUBnormal series (each term normal in the next, not necessarily in G) with all factors ≅ ℤ; modules are left kG-modules with kG = MonoidAlgebra k G; 'free' is Module.Free (automatically finite rank given Module.Finite over the nontrivial ring kG); 'is an ideal' = isomorphic as a kG-module to a left ideal (Mathlib `Ideal`). The left/right choice is immaterial for group rings via the anti-automorphism g ↦ g⁻¹. 'Either … or' is read inclusively. G, k, P are quantified over `Type` following the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25); no generality lost since poly-ℤ groups are countable and f.g. modules over a Type-0 ring have Type-0 representatives. No candidate omitted the slot and no candidate raised decomposition objections. The bespoke IsPolyZ definition lives in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean); a maintainer may prefer moving it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
